## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kassapamandiyajātaka* (Ja 312) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection, rendered into English as *Foolish Youth*. According to the framing narrative of the commentary, the Buddha delivered the teaching while residing at Jetavana monastery, occasioned by an aged monk (*mahallakabhikkhu*) [Fausböll 1883].

In the story of the past, an ascetic father and a younger brother argue along the road, leading the Bodhisatta to reprove them on the virtues of reconciliation and responsibility [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1883]. The Bodhisatta's verses emphasize that virtuous persons reconcile quickly when disputes arise, and that a true friend remains heedful, avoids seeking dissension or faults, and does not cast off companions [Anandajoti 2010]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the elderly ascetic father was the aged elder, the younger ascetic was a novice (*sāmaṇera*), and the admonishing Bodhisatta was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].
